Definition: from G68 and G832 (in the sense of G833); to camp out:--abide in the field.
BiblicalUsage: Agrauleo means to camp out — to abide in the field — and it appears once, in the Christmas story: 'there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.' The word holds the whole scene: men sleeping rough under the sky, on duty in the dark, when the angel came. The first to hear of the Saviour's birth were men camping out with sheep.
TheologicalSignificance: Shepherds abiding in the field heard the good news first, and this word only says they were out there — the angels did the preaching.
